text:
[SECTION 2. ESTABLISHMENT AND INSTITUTIONAL HISTORY]
Established: 1956 (homepage: "Established in 1956 by the V. Rangaswamy Naidu Educational Trust (VRET)"). History text (About Us page, "The Management"): "Established in 1956 in Coimbatore, the V. Rangaswamy Naidu Educational Trust (VRET) is dedicated to advancing technical education in Tamil Nadu. Founded by visionary industrialists and philanthropists Prof. R. Venkataswamy Naidu and Prof. P. R. Ramakrishnan, the Trust launched the Coimbatore Institute of Technology (CIT) in 1956, followed by the CIT Sandwich Polytechnic College in 1961." Leadership history as published: - Prof. R. Venkataswamy Naidu served as Correspondent from 1956 to 1994. - Prof. P. R. Ramakrishnan was Founder-Principal for 25 years and served as Correspondent for 12 years. - Dr. S. R. K. Prasad took the helm as Managing Trustee in 2008, followed by Sri S. Rajiv Rangasami. Former Correspondents panel (same page): - Sri. R. Venkataswamy Naidu (1956 - 1994), B.Sc.(Tech) Manchester, Founder Correspondent - Prof. P. R. Ramakrishnan (1994-2008), M.S.(M.I.T) USA, M.B.A., F.I.E., Founder Principal, Former Member of Parliament - Dr. S. R. K. Prasad (2008-2021), D.Sc.(USA), FORSI, Managing Trustee, VRET Chairman, Governing Council, CIT

document_title: College Overview and Autonomous Administration
text:
[SECTION 3. VISION, MISSION AND OBJECTIVES]
Mission (About Us page): "The mission of CIT is to 'impart high quality education and training to its students to make them World-Class Engineers with a foresight to the changes and problems, and pioneers to offer innovative solutions to benefit the nation and the world at large'." (Homepage wording differs slightly in capitalisation: "Impart high quality education and training to its students to make them world-class engineers with a foresight to the changes and problems, and pioneers who offer innovative solutions to benefit the nation and the world at large".) Vision (About Us page): "The Institute strives to inculcate sound engineering knowledge along with a strong realization of social responsibilities, enabling students to address current and emerging national challenges and contribute their expertise to the global arena." (Homepage wording: "The Institute strives to inculcate a sound knowledge in engineering along with a realization of social responsibilities to enable its students to combat the current and impending challenges faced by our country and to extend their expertise to the global arena.") Core Values (About Us page): 1. Aiding Social Advancements through Technologies - technologies are instruments for promoting individuals and society; curricula, syllabi and teaching-learning methods aim at holistic progress and societal uplift. 2. Employability for Students - the Institution strives to mould students as qualified manpower through deeper knowledge, critical skills and transferable competencies. 3. Quality Education - ensured through quality teaching, state-of-the-art infrastructure, research and development, curricula in cutting-edge technologies, industry-institution interaction, a healthy academic ambience, co-curricular and extracurricular activities including internships. 4. Appreciation of Intellectual Excellence - intellectual accomplishments of students and faculty recognised; numerous endowment awards instituted. 5. Transparency, Accountability and Empathy - core values embedded in the administration. Separate "Objectives" statement: Not found in the inspected official sources.

text:
[SECTION 4. INSTITUTIONAL PROFILE AND OFFICIAL DESCRIPTION]
Homepage description ("Developing Future-ready Graduates"): "Established in 1956 by the V. Rangaswamy Naidu Educational Trust (VRET), Coimbatore Institute of Technology (CIT) stands as one of Tamil Nadu's most respected and sought-after institutions. An autonomous institution since 1987, CIT is proudly affiliated with Anna University, Chennai. Our vibrant 69-acre campus is home to 14 departments. We offer a wide range of programmes, from traditional engineering and cutting-edge digital technologies to five-year integrated M.Sc. degrees, MCA, and MBA programmes." "CIT is defined by a legacy of excellence. Our teaching methods don't just follow trends, they prepare graduates to be future-ready, technically skilled, and socially responsible. This commitment is reflected in our exceptional placement record, with top-tier multinationals and innovative startups consistently recruiting CITians." Meta description (homepage): "Coimbatore Institute of Technology (CIT) is a top engineering college in Coimbatore offering quality education, research, innovation, and placements." Programme groupings as published on the homepage cards (https://cit.edu.in/): - Engineering: B.E. Civil Engineering; B.E. Mechanical Engineering; B.E. Electrical & Electronics Engineering; B.E. Electronics & Communication Engineering; B.E. Computer Science & Engineering; B.Tech. Information Technology; B.Tech. Chemical Engineering; B.Tech. Artificial Intelligence and Data Science; B.E. Electronics Engineering (VLSI Design and Technology) - Science & Humanities: Humanities; Mathematics; Physics; Chemistry - Integrated Programmes (five-year): M.Sc Software Systems; M.Sc Data Science; M.Sc Decision & Computing Sciences; M.Sc Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning - PG Programmes: Business Administration (MBA); Computer Application (MCA); M.E. Construction Management Other departments listed in navigation: Library; Physical Education; COE (Exam); MMTTC. CONFLICT FLAG: The homepage text says "14 departments". The navigation lists 8 engineering + 6 PG + 4 science/humanities programme/department links (18), and the homepage cards additionally list B.E. Electronics Engineering (VLSI Design and Technology) and M.E. Construction Management, which are absent from the navigation menu. The "14 departments" figure is not reconciled here.

text:
[SECTION 7. CAMPUS FACILITIES AND INFRASTRUCTURE]
Infrastructure index (official page lists): General Facilities; Academic Facilities; Hostel Facilities; Wellness Hub; Sports Facilities; Internet Facility; Library Facility; Digital Library; Help Desk; Blogs; Water Conservation Facilities; Centre for E-Learning; Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Centre. General Facilities page (https://cit.edu.in/general-facilities) - "Facility Management System at CIT": - Sustainability and water: rainwater harvesting network across all major buildings; Sewage Water Treatment Plant (STP) using biological treatment; a wastewater treatment facility to recycle water for non-potable uses such as gardening and irrigation. - Facilities for differently-abled (Barrier Free Environment): ramp, lift, wheelchair and disabled-friendly washrooms in all buildings; lift arrangement in all blocks; ramps in all buildings and all laboratories; wheelchairs and left-hand chairs for students who require them; separate toilets for physically challenged students. - Energy and infrastructure: solar photovoltaic panels on rooftops; centralised Power House with generators and transformers for 24/7 backup for laboratories, hostels and administrative blocks; fully furnished Guest House for visiting professors, industrial experts and parents. - Campus essential services: multi-cuisine canteen; 24/7 in-house ATM; on-campus health center with qualified medical staff, first-aid equipment and emergency transport services. - Gym and Sports Facility sections exist with images only (no text). Academic Facilities page (https://cit.edu.in/life-at-cit/academic-facilities), Wellness Hub, Internet facility (IT Resource Maintenance Cell), E-Learning Centre, Water Conservation page: Not found in the inspected official sources (not opened). Seminar-hall excerpt from an official NAAC-related PDF (https://cit.edu.in/uploads/epdf_documents/4764bcd0e384855f777fa1bcf84e2989.pdf, undated): lists ICT-enabled seminar halls (e.g., Main Block departmental seminar halls for ECE, Mechanical, EEE and Civil; IT Block AC seminar halls IT003, IT211, IT212), each with "Projector, Screen, Wi-Fi & LAN". Laboratory list not extracted.

- Listed on: Departments page (under "PG Programmes"); homepage (under "Integrated Programmes"); Admission Requirements ("Five-year Integrated Programmes"); M.Sc. Brochure 2026. - Department-page URLs: Software Systems https://cit.edu.in/msc-software-systems | Data Science https://cit.edu.in/msc-data-science | Decision and Computing Sciences https://cit.edu.in/msc-decision-and-computing-sciences | AI and Machine Learning https://cit.edu.in/msc-artificial-intelligence-and-machine-learning (only the Software Systems page was opened). - "Since" years (M.Sc. Brochure 2026): Software Systems 1998; Data Science 2016; Decision and Computing Sciences 2017; Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning 2019. Eligibility: M.Sc. Software Systems / Data Science / AI and Machine Learning (admission page and M.Sc. Brochure 2026 agree) - A pass in HSC (or equivalent) examination with Mathematics, Physics, and Chemistry as subjects is required. - Candidates (other than SC/ST) must have a minimum aggregate of 70% in Mathematics + Physics + (Chemistry or Computer Science). - Note (as published): this does not mean 70% in each subject individually; the requirement is based on the total combined marks. Example given: out of 300 marks (100 per subject), a minimum of 210 marks in total. Eligibility: M.Sc. Decision and Computing Sciences - A pass in HSC (or equivalent) examination with Mathematics, Physics, and Chemistry as subjects; candidates (other than SC/ST) must have a minimum aggregate of 70% in Mathematics + Physics + (Chemistry or Computer Science) (OR) - A pass in HSC / equivalent exam with one subject from Category A and two subjects from Category B as the subjects of study. CATEGORY A - Mathematics / Applied Mathematics / Statistics / Business Mathematics / Business Mathematics & Statistics. CATEGORY B - Commerce / Economics / Accountancy / Computer Science. Candidates (other than SC/ST) with an aggregate of 70% and above in the three subjects in total, one from Category A and two from Category B, only need to apply. Admission process (admission page): two-stage evaluation - (1) marks obtained in the Higher Secondary qualifying board examination; (2) an institute-level entrance examination ("internal entrance test conducted by the institute"). "Note: The examination center is located only in Coimbatore."

text:
[5.2 Eligibility - M.Sc. Decision and Computing Sciences (DCS) (programme-specific; two routes)]
Route 1: - A pass in HSC (or equivalent) with Mathematics, Physics, and Chemistry as subjects. - Candidates (other than SC/ST) must have a minimum aggregate of 70% in Mathematics + Physics + (Chemistry or Computer Science). Route 2 (OR): - A pass in HSC / equivalent exam with one subject from Category A and two subjects from Category B as the subjects of study. CATEGORY A - Mathematics / Applied Mathematics / Statistics / Business Mathematics / Business Mathematics & Statistics. CATEGORY B - Commerce / Economics / Accountancy / Computer Science. - Candidates (other than SC/ST) with an aggregate of 70% and above in the three subjects in total (one from Category A and two from Category B) only need to apply. Source: https://cit.edu.in/admission/financial-aids (academic year not stated) and the Aided call-letter PDF. - The page states that the institute facilitates "more than 24 government and private scholarship schemes" for undergraduate students. - Guidelines: scholarship applications on the prescribed forms to the Principal's Office within 30 days of the institute reopening or the date of admission, whichever is later; all certificates and documents enclosed (incomplete submissions not considered); a student may receive only one scholarship or fee concession at a time; continuation subject to the minimum attendance percentage stipulated by the University; serious misconduct (including strikes or ragging) results in immediate cancellation of benefits. - Government-sponsored schemes named: Adi Dravidar Welfare Scholarships (General and Higher Education Special); Backward Class (BC) Welfare Scholarships; Tamil Nadu Minority Merit-cum-Means Scholarship; Tamil Nadu Farmer Social Security Welfare Scholarship; Chief Minister's Scholarship and Arignar Anna Award; interstate scholarships (Pondicherry, Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Meghalaya, Shillong, Arunachal Pradesh, Tripura, Nagaland, Mizoram); AICTE Pragathi Scheme (women students); Physically Handicapped Scholarship and AICTE Saksham Scheme (differently-abled students); scholarships for children of teachers, defense personnel, ex-servicemen and deceased government employees; Gandhi Memorial and Merit-cum-Means Scholarships. - Mandatory fee concessions (as per Rule 92 - MER): students admitted under Government-Aided programmes are eligible for a full tuition fee waiver if they belong to Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), or Converted Christians from SC/ST communities; "This concession is granted irrespective of the family's annual income." - Private/trust-funded: Tamil Nadu Educational Trust; Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC); Siragugal Scholarship Scheme. - Scholarship values, eligibility conditions and forms: "students are encouraged to visit the Institute Office." (Not published on the page.) - First Graduate concession: a "First Graduate Concession - Declaration Form" is included in the Aided PDF. It requires TNEA/TNLEA application number, year of admission, college code, branch, First Graduate Certificate number, and details of family members (name, relationship, age, educational qualification, EMIS number of class 10th/11th/12th, whether ID proof attached). The declaration states liability for criminal prosecution and "return the amount equal to three time the tuition fee waived" if information is false. The concession's monetary scope is not stated in the PDF. - Home page links "Scholarships" to https://cit.edu.in/students/scholarship (not opened).

text:
[4. EXAMINATION ADMINISTRATION AND PROCEDURES]
Source: https://cit.edu.in/coe/about-the-office-of-the-controller-of-examinations The Office of the Controller of Examinations (COE) "plays a vital role in safeguarding the academic credibility of the Institute. It is responsible for planning, administering, and monitoring all examination-related activities, ensuring that assessment processes are conducted with fairness, accuracy, and transparency." Key responsibilities listed on the page: - Conduct of Examinations: planning and administering all internal and end-semester examinations in accordance with the approved academic schedule for every programme. - Appointment of Examiners: identifying and appointing competent faculty members and external experts for question paper preparation and theory paper evaluation. - Assessment of Practical and Project Work: constituting specialized Examination Committees to evaluate laboratory examinations, project reviews, and viva-voce assessments. - Result Compilation and Declaration: processing, verification and finalization of results, followed by official publication after approval by the Result Passing Board (RPB). - Issue of Academic Records: official grade sheets and academic statements. - Academic Reporting: performance analysis reports presented to the Academic Council. - Recommendation for Degree Award: verifying eligibility and recommending qualified candidates for degrees. Additional services: certified transcripts and duplicate academic records; verification of certificates and mark statements; organizing the Annual Graduation Day. Office administration: headed by the Controller of Examinations, assisted by a Deputy Controller, supported by thirteen staff members. document_title: Placements, Recruiters, Statistics and Career Guidance
text:
[1. PLACEMENT CELL OVERVIEW AND RESPONSIBILITIES]
Source: https://cit.edu.in/placements/placement-cell The Institute has a Placement Cell headed by a staff member holding the rank of a Professor. The Cell is actively involved in securing placements for students graduating from the Institute. The office maintains close associations with industrial establishments. These establishments conduct pre-placement presentations and campus interviews, and select student representatives from each department to coordinate placement activities. The Placement Cell provides facilities to conduct group discussions, tests, and interviews. It also has a library and a communication lab to enhance students' general aptitude and communication skills. The official page states that national and multinational companies visit the Institute every year for campus recruitment, and that several reputed companies seek to be the "Day One" recruiter for each academic year. Information regarding campus recruitment is regularly displayed to students to help them plan their careers and understand the industries approaching the Institute. At the beginning of the academic year, a general body meeting is conducted for final-year students interested in placement activities. Monthly review meetings are convened to plan future activities. The Cell coordinates pre-placement activities for senior and junior students and motivates students to pursue higher studies by supporting preparation for competitive examinations such as GATE, TOEFL, GRE, CAT, and GMAT. The Cell also seeks to promote self-employment by facilitating government-supported financial assistance through the banking sector. Workshops are organized to develop students' entrepreneurial potential.

text:
[2.2 National Resource Centre (NRC)  -  Structural Engineering]
Source: National Resource Centre (NRC) URL: https://cit.edu.in/others/nrc The page describes the National Resource Centre (NRC) for Structural Engineering at CIT as a national-level platform for advanced academic engagement, capacity building and applied research. It states that the centre was established with the support of the Ministry of Education, Government of India. Objectives stated: - Knowledge sharing on structural analysis, design methodologies and construction materials. - Faculty capacity building through Annual Refresher Programmes in Teaching (ARPIT), faculty development programmes and domain-specific training workshops. - Awareness of updated Indian Standards (IS codes) and internationally accepted design practices. - Development of digital learning resources, recorded lectures and online modules. Focus areas stated: - High-performance, self-compacting and advanced concrete materials - Earthquake engineering, seismic assessment and retrofitting techniques - Steel - concrete composite systems for modern infrastructure - Smart materials, sensors and structural health monitoring systems - Sustainable construction practices and life-cycle assessment - Computational mechanics, including finite element modeling and AI-based structural performance prediction Facilities/resources stated: - Structural Engineering Laboratory, equipped with high-capacity loading systems and advanced testing instruments. - Digital Content Development Facility for recording online courses, expert lectures and interactive webinars. - High-Performance Computing Facilities with access to STAAD, SAP2000, ANSYS and ABAQUS. - Library resources including national and international journals, reference books and updated design standards.

text:
[4. LIBRARY FACILITIES, HOURS AND ONLINE RESOURCES]
Current library navigation/source: https://cit.edu.in/library/about Library overview: The library was established in 1956 and is adjacent to the main building. The current page gives the area as 13,381 square feet (1,243 square meters). It supports access to physical and digital resources. Library services/navigation: https://cit.edu.in/library/ The official library section links to: - About - Library Staff Details - Kalam Knowledge Club - Digital Library - Web OPAC - E-Resources - Services - Sections - Collections - Institutional Membership - Downloads - Rules and Regulations - Layout - Virtual Tour - Links - Contact Us E-resources/off-campus access: https://idp.cit.edu.in/ The official CIT library off-campus access page states that faculty members, research scholars and students have credentials for remote access to subscribed e-resources 24/7. Users who have not received login details are directed to library@cit.edu.in. The page lists e-books, databases and e-journals, including McGraw Hill, Scopus, ASCE Journals Online, ASME Journals Online, EBSCO, Elsevier ScienceDirect, IEEE Xplore and Springer. Library opening hours: An official PDF titled "LIBRARY" at https://cit.edu.in/uploads/epdf_documents/8e7c826bf2ddd07adbea376368fbf334.pdf publishes the following hours: - Monday to Friday: 9.00 a.m. - 7.00 p.m. - Saturday: 9.00 a.m. - 3.00 p.m. - Vacation: 9.30 a.m. - 4.30 p.m. - Closed on Sundays and Government holidays. Caution: this is an older official PDF (search indexing indicates it was crawled several years ago). The currently inspected library pages do not independently confirm these hours. Treat the schedule as historically published, not independently verified as current; contact library@cit.edu.in before relying on it.

For mixed-gender groups, a female faculty member is mandatory. This concerns industrial visits and does not establish a general daily student bus service. document_title: Campus Facilities, Library, Hostels, Transport and FAQs
text:
[7. ACCESSIBILITY, SECURITY AND VISITOR INFORMATION]
Accessibility source: https://cit.edu.in/general-facilities/ The official General Facilities page states that the institute provides a barrier-free environment, including: - Lift arrangements in all blocks of the campus - Ramps in all buildings and laboratories - Wheelchairs for students who require them - "Left hand Chairs provided for require students" (wording as published on the page) - Separate toilets for physically challenged students Visitor accommodation source: https://cit.edu.in/general-facilities/ The page states that CIT maintains a fully furnished Guest House with modern amenities for visiting professors, industrial experts and parents. Booking process, rates, availability and guest-house contact details were not found in the inspected page. Security/entry source: https://cit.edu.in/others/sop The official SOP page says all entry and exit points are monitored continuously and access is permitted after verification of valid identification for students, staff and visitors. Security personnel conduct routine patrols across academic blocks, hostels, laboratories and common areas. A separate official security document indexed at https://cit.edu.in/uploads/epdf_documents/520554b01edbafd290cf6a3da16208cf.pdf includes internal gate/security instructions. These include recording outsiders without ID cards in registers, restrictions on entry by other college students, and references to students leaving after 7.00 pm and the main gate being closed after evening-class students leave by 9 pm. This appears to be an internal security document and may be time-sensitive; do not treat it as a current public visitor policy without confirmation. Public visitor registration procedure, visiting hours, parking instructions and a visitor-specific phone number: Not found in the inspected official sources. Contact the central office or Help Desk before visiting.

Autonomous-status date conflict: AQAR 2022-23 reports 01/06/1987, while AQAR 2023-24 reports 08/07/1987. Preserve both values and cite the reporting year. 2. Autonomy-cycle issue: the 2021 UGC extension letter covers sessions 2021-22 through 2025-26; it should not be used alone to establish the 2026-27 status. 3. Syllabus versions: CIT exposes historical and newer curricula concurrently. Regulation/admission cohort must be stored as metadata. 4. Current versus legacy student rules: legacy Code of Conduct, current Rules & Regulations, and current HTML Code of Conduct coexist. 5. Current fee information is on HTML pages; no verified PDF was found during this inspection. 6. Current annual-report page did not expose PDF URLs in the returned page content; no annual-report PDF URL was invented. 7. Course brochures are current 2026 documents, while several syllabus/regulatory PDFs are 2021-2024 or older. A RAG system should use publication/applicability year as a retrieval filter. document_title: CIT Academic Regulations & Exam Rules 2026
text:
[Page 1]
CIT ACADEMIC REGULATIONS & EXAM RULES 2026 Coimbatore Institute of Technology - Autonomous Regulations 1. Attendance Regulations: - Minimum required attendance is 75% aggregate across all registered courses in a semester. - Condonation for shortage (65% to 74%) may be sanctioned by the Principal for genuine medical grounds. - Students below 65% attendance are detained and must repeat the semester. 2. Choice Based Credit System (CBCS): - Total credits required for B.E. / B.Tech degree: 160 - 165 Credits. - Grading System: O (10), A+ (9), A (8), B+ (7), B (6), C (5), RA (Re-appear/Fail, <45 Marks). - Evaluation: 40% Continuous Assessment (CAT 1 & CAT 2) + 60% End Semester Exam.

text:
[Page 1]
COIMBATORE INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY (CIT) Official Institutional Overview & Autonomous Governance 2026 Coimbatore Institute of Technology (CIT), Peelamedu, Coimbatore - 641014, Tamil Nadu. Established in 1956 by V. Rangaswamy Naidu Educational Trust (VRET). Affiliated to Anna University, Approved by AICTE, Accredited by NAAC with 'A' Grade. Granted Autonomous status in 1987 by UGC and Anna University. Motto: Progress Through Technology. Official Contact: Phone 0422-2574071 | Email: principal@cit.edu.in | Website: www.cit.edu.in Key Academic Highlights: - Offering 9 B.E./B.Tech programs, 12 M.E./M.Tech programs, MCA, 5-Yr Integrated M.Sc. - Over 200+ experienced faculty members with high research citations. - Active MoUs with Bosch, Texas Instruments, Qualcomm, IBM, TCS, L&T, and Caterpillar. - 25+ Acre Lush Green Autonomous Campus located along Avinashi Road in Peelamedu, Coimbatore.
